provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Composition 1
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to
state who their best friend is
list three qualities of their friend
write four simple sentences
read their composition aloud

Introduction:
We all have friends in class.
Today we write about our best friend.

Content:
A composition is a short piece of writing.
We write four sentences about our best friend.
First sentence: My best friend is [name].
Second sentence: My friend is kind.
Third sentence: We play together.
Fourth sentence: I love my friend.

Class activity:
Each pupil draws a picture of their friend.
Then they write four sentences about the picture.

Evaluation questions:
Who is your best friend?
What does your friend like to do?
Can you read your sentences?
What is a composition?

Summary:
Today we wrote about our best friend.

topics.title: Composition 2
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to
state their favourite food
list ingredients of the food
write four descriptive sentences
explain why they like it

Introduction:
We all eat different foods at home.
Today we write about our favourite food.

Content:
A composition tells about something special.
We write four sentences about our favourite food.
First sentence: My favourite food is [name].
Second sentence: It has rice and fish.
Third sentence: It smells very nice.
Fourth sentence: I eat it every Sunday.

Class activity:
Pupils bring food pictures from home.
They write four sentences about their food picture.

Evaluation questions:
What is your favourite food?
Why do you like this food?
Can you describe its colour?
What ingredients does it have?

Summary:
We wrote about our favourite food today.

topics.title: Composition 3
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to
state what happens on a rainy day
list three rain activities
write a story with beginning, middle, end
read their story aloud

Introduction:
We know rain comes during harmattan season.
Today we write about a rainy day.

Content:
A story has three parts.
First: It started to rain heavily.
Then: We played in the puddles.
Last: We drank hot chocolate at home.
We use first, then, last words.

Class activity:
Pupils make rain sounds with hands.
Then they write three sentences about rainy day fun.

Evaluation questions:
What does rain sound like?
What do you do when it rains?
Can you tell first, then, last?
What do we drink on rainy days?

Summary:
We wrote our first rainy day story.

topics.title: Letter writing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to
state how to start a letter
list two things to tell granny
write a simple letter with greeting and closing
read their letter aloud

Introduction:
We love our grannies very much.
Today we write a letter to our granny.

Content:
A letter has a greeting and closing.
Greeting: Dear Granny,
Closing: Love from [name]
We write simple sentences inside.
Tell granny about school and friends.

Class activity:
Pupils fold paper to make letter shape.
They write to their imaginary granny.

Evaluation questions:
How do we start a letter?
What do we write at the end?
What can you tell your granny?
How do we close a letter?

Summary:
We learned to write a letter.

topics.title: List making
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to
state what a list is
list items for shopping
write neat numbered lists
read their list aloud

Introduction:
Mamas go to market to buy things.
Today we make our own shopping list.

Content:
A list helps us remember things.
We write numbers before each item.
Example:
1. Rice
2. Beans
3. Plantain
We can also make wish lists.

Class activity:
Pupils play shopkeeper game.
They make lists of items to buy.

Evaluation questions:
What is a list?
Why do we use numbers?
What would you buy at market?
Can you read your list?

Summary:
We learned to make numbered lists.

topics.title: Card messages
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to
state when we give cards
write birthday wishes
write thank you messages
read their messages aloud

Introduction:
We give cards on special days.
Today we write messages inside cards.

Content:
Cards have messages for friends.
Birthday message: Happy birthday to you!
Thank you message: Thank you for my gift.
We write neatly inside the card.

Class activity:
Pupils make birthday cards from paper.
They write nice messages inside.

Evaluation questions:
When do we give cards?
What do we write for birthdays?
What do we write for thanks?
Where do we write messages?

Summary:
We wrote messages for cards.

topics.title: Label and caption
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to
state what a label is
write labels for objects
write captions for pictures
read their labels aloud

Introduction:
We see labels everywhere in market.
Today we learn to write labels and captions.

Content:
A label tells what something is.
Example: Mango
A caption tells about a picture.
Example: Big yellow mango
We write short and clear words.

Class activity:
Pupils draw classroom objects.
They write labels for their drawings.

Evaluation questions:
What is a label?
What is a caption?
Can you label your drawing?
Can you caption your picture?

Summary:
We learned to write labels and captions.

topics.title: Dictation mastery
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to
listen carefully to teacher
write dictated sentences correctly
check their own work
read their paragraph aloud

Introduction:
We hear sounds all around us.
Today we practice writing what we hear.

Content:
Dictation means writing what you hear.
Teacher reads a paragraph slowly.
Pupils write each word as they hear it.
Then they check their own work.

Class activity:
Pupils close eyes and listen.
Teacher reads: The cat is fat.
Pupils write exactly what they hear.

Evaluation questions:
What is dictation?
Why do we check our work?
Can you write what you hear?
Can you read your paragraph?

Summary:
We practiced dictation today.

topics.title: Free writing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to
choose what to write about
write freely about their choice
share their writing with class
read their writing aloud

Introduction:
We all have different things we like.
Today we write about anything we choose.

Content:
Free writing means writing what you want.
You can write about family, toys, or food.
Write as many sentences as you can.
There are no wrong answers in free writing.

Class activity:
Pupils sit in a circle.
Each pupil shares one thing they wrote about.

Evaluation questions:
What did you choose to write about?
Why did you choose that topic?
Can you read what you wrote?
What is free writing?

Summary:
We wrote about what we like.

topics.title: Revision and author chair
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to
read their writing clearly
sit in author chair
receive author certificate
share their favorite writing

Introduction:
We have learned many writing skills.
Today we celebrate our writing journey.

Content:
Author chair is a special chair.
Pupils sit in author chair to read.
They read their best writing aloud.
Teacher gives author certificates.

Class activity:
Pupils take turns in author chair.
Each reads their favorite composition.
Class claps for each author.

Evaluation questions:
What is author chair?
Can you read your writing clearly?
How do we celebrate writing?
What did you learn this term?

Summary:
We celebrated our writing growth.
